name: std/time
description: Time: the calendar and its formatting, the high-resolution counter, the stopwatch, and timers.
residual: Time arrived 2026-09-03 and closes the two holes named here. Both clocks were reachable and neither was usable: PrecisionTimer.GetCounter is monotonic on both hosts but counts nanoseconds on Unix and QueryPerformanceCounter ticks on Windows, so every caller carried its own division; and Dates.Now is the wall clock in local time with nothing saying which local. Time gives the monotonic clock one unit everywhere and the wall clock an origin -- 1970-01-01 UTC -- plus the host offset from Clock.tz. There is still no IANA zone database: naming a zone, or asking what a past date offset was, needs one.

Created 2026-08-27. In: Dates from std/base, the clocks from std/system. Clock stays in std/runtime -- the kernel needs it before any library does. Missing and worth adding: monotonic time and a timezone database; the calendar itself (Dates) is already complete.
